project.name: TradePulse (Example Project)
project.oneSentenceIdea: [EXAMPLE] Exclusive SMS job dispatch alerts with 1-click booking for solo plumbing and HVAC contractors.
project.targetMarket: Solo trade contractors (1-3 crew) in Austin & Dallas TX (Example Cohort)
project.problemStatement: [EXAMPLE] Solo contractors waste $600-$1,200/mo on shared lead brokers like Angi and Thumbtack that sell the same unvetted lead to 5 contractors simultaneously, resulting in a <15% win rate and hours wasted on phone tag.
project.targetUserGroup: Licensed residential plumbers & HVAC technicians with 1-3 vans
project.currentAlternatives: Angi leads ($80/lead, non-exclusive), Google Local Service Ads, manual word-of-mouth texts, Craigslist postings.
project.successDefinition: Contractors receive guaranteed pre-booked appointments directly to their calendar with customer payment method pre-authorized on file.
project.behavioralChange: Contractors stop manually cold-calling leads between jobs and instead accept dispatches with a single SMS reply "1".
project.willingnessToPayTrigger: Contractors will pay $25 per booked dispatch, or 8% of completed invoice, because it guarantees zero bidding time.
project.founderSkills: Ex-field service dispatcher (5 yrs) + full-stack web developer. Direct access to 25 local contractor contacts.

evidence.claim: [EXAMPLE CLAIM] Solo trade contractors lose over 6 hours every week calling shared leads that never pick up.
evidence.evidenceNotes: [EXAMPLE NOTES] Simulated discovery data: 6 synthetic discovery calls with plumbers reporting 14% callback rates.
evidence.nextTest: Collect call logs from 3 pilot contractors over 1 week.

evidence.claim: [EXAMPLE CLAIM] Contractors are willing to pay a flat fee per completed booking rather than upfront lead bidding.
evidence.evidenceNotes: [EXAMPLE NOTES] 4 out of 5 example contractor profiles agreed they would pay $25-$40 per pre-scheduled job.
evidence.nextTest: Pre-sell 5 paid test bookings via concierge manual dispatch.

evidence.claim: [EXAMPLE CLAIM] Homeowners will input credit cards to book emergency plumbing visits online.
evidence.evidenceNotes: [EXAMPLE NOTES] Untested hypothesis. Homeowners may hesitate to pre-authorize payment before speaking to a technician.
evidence.nextTest: Run a simple smoke test page offering $50 diagnostic deposit.

evidence.claim: [EXAMPLE CLAIM] Contractors can respond to incoming SMS alerts in under 90 seconds while on job sites.
evidence.evidenceNotes: [EXAMPLE NOTES] Critical assumption: If response time is >10 mins, homeowners will cancel or call a competitor.
evidence.nextTest: Simulate 10 mock SMS alerts during work hours and measure response latency.

research.title: [EXAMPLE SOURCE] IBISWorld US Plumbers Industry Report 2025
research.summary: [EXAMPLE SUMMARY] US plumbing industry is $134B, with 68% of firms having fewer than 4 employees.
keyFindings: Average job ticket for residential emergency is $340-$550.
High fragmentation: solo operators rely primarily on referral and local lead brokers.

competitors.name: Angi (formerly Angie's List)
competitors.productDescription: Massive home service directory selling leads to multiple contractors.
competitors.targetAudience: Medium to large contracting firms with dedicated sales reps
competitors.positioning: Largest brand name in homeowner service discovery
weaknesses: Tons of tire-kicker leads that never answer
customerComplaints: [EXAMPLE QUOTE] Paid $1,200 this month and got 1 real job
[EXAMPLE QUOTE] Leads are cold or already hired someone else 3 days ago
competitors.keyDifferentiators: 100% exclusive dispatches, zero monthly subscription, pay only on confirmed bookings.
competitors.evidenceNotes: [EXAMPLE NOTES] Examined 45 1-star Trustpilot reviews from contractors in Q3 2025.

competitors.name: Thumbtack
competitors.productDescription: Bidding marketplace where contractors pay when customers reach out.
competitors.targetAudience: Solo freelancers and local trade businesses
competitors.positioning: Flexible quote marketplace with instant matching
weaknesses: Contractors pay even if customer ghosted after first text
Customer price shopping drives margins down
customerComplaints: [EXAMPLE QUOTE] Charged $35 for an inquiry that never replied to my quote
[EXAMPLE QUOTE] Race to the bottom on pricing
competitors.keyDifferentiators: Pre-vetted jobs with price minimums; no charges for unconfirmed inquiries.
competitors.evidenceNotes: [EXAMPLE NOTES] Feedback aggregated from example contractor interview scripts.

experiments.resultSummary: [EXAMPLE OUTCOME] 9 contractors replied with interest; 7 signed up for the pilot SMS phone tree. Hypothesis validated!
experiments.decisionTaken: Proceed to concierge dispatch test with first 5 contractors.

experiments.resultSummary: [EXAMPLE OUTCOME] Currently running local neighborhood flyer & Nextdoor test. 6 starts, 2 booked.

interviews.participantRole: Solo owner-operator (1 helper, 2 vans), 11 years in business
interviews.objectives: Understand lead acquisition pain and current spend on Angi / Google LSA.
interviews.notesOrTranscript: [EXAMPLE TRANSCRIPT] Marcus spends $950/month on Angi. Says he wins maybe 2 jobs a month from it because 4 other guys get the same lead. He is on a job site with his head under a sink and can't stop to text people within 30 seconds.
recurringPainPoints: Phone tag while physically doing labor
interviews.existingWorkarounds: Hired part-time virtual assistant to reply to Angi texts ($400/mo), but still loses jobs.
interviews.willingnessToPayNotes: Stated directly: "If you give me a job that's already scheduled for tomorrow at 10am with a card on file, take $40 right out of the top, I don't care."
verbatimQuotes: [EXAMPLE QUOTE] "I am paying Angi $950 a month just to get ghosted by people looking for a $20 handyman."
[EXAMPLE QUOTE] "If the job is locked in and exclusive, take your cut. Just don't sell it to Dave down the street too."
interviews.surprisesOrObjections: Contractor prefers SMS only; will not download another heavy app on his phone.

landingPage.headline: Stop Chasing Dead Leads. Get Booked Jobs Sent to Your Phone via SMS.
landingPage.subheadline: Exclusive emergency plumbing jobs dispatched directly to your SMS. No bidding against 5 other plumbers. No monthly fees. Reply "1" to claim.
landingPage.problemHeadline: Angi Charges You $80 Just to Play Phone Tag With Ghost Leads
landingPage.problemBody: You are with your head under a sink doing actual labor. By the time you wipe your hands to text an Angi lead, four other guys already called them, or they were just looking for a $20 handyman. TradePulse only alerts you when a customer has a credit card authorized and a confirmed address.
landingPage.step1: Homeowner requests emergency help with card on file.
landingPage.step2: We text the job details to your phone. Reply "1" to accept.
landingPage.step3: Job is booked exclusively to your calendar. You keep 100% of your labor fee.
landingPage.faq1Q: How is this different from Angi or Thumbtack?
landingPage.faq1A: We never sell the same lead to multiple contractors. When you get an alert, you are the only technician with the reservation window.
landingPage.faq2A: Zero monthly subscription. You only pay a flat $25 dispatch fee when you successfully confirm a scheduled job.

decisions.title: [EXAMPLE DECISION] Reject native mobile app in favor of Twilio SMS
decisions.rationale: Contractor interviews demonstrated refusal to download and login to mobile apps while wearing work gloves. SMS has 98% open rate in <3 minutes.
decisions.rejectedAlternatives: React Native mobile app with push notifications; web portal.

risks.title: [EXAMPLE RISK] Homeowner cancellation if dispatch takes >15 minutes
risks.evidenceNotes: Emergency plumbing buyers call the next plumber if no confirmation is received quickly.
risks.mitigation: Implement tiered SMS broadcast: alert 3 contractors simultaneously in a 5-mile radius, first to reply gets it.
risks.nextTest: Simulate contractor SMS reply speeds during working hours.

risks.title: [EXAMPLE RISK] Disintermediation (contractor and homeowner deal off-platform)
risks.evidenceNotes: Once contractor has homeowner contact, future repeat work bypasses TradePulse.
risks.mitigation: Charge flat fee on initial dispatch rather than ongoing maintenance commissions.
risks.nextTest: Survey pilot contractors on preferred billing model.
